meta.title: Claude Haiku 5.5 · AI/ML · community · run 2
meta.note: Main run, 60 minutes. The verifier accepted 2 of 4 credited claims; 2 set a new best held-out result on their dataset. Verdicts from the re-run of the official verifier.

agents.brief: You work on AG News topic classification (4 classes). Data: $DATA_DIR/agnews/train.csv (columns id,text,target). No internet, no pretrained models. Goal: a 'prediction' contribution whose predictions beat the baseline in /lab/data/baselines (TF-IDF 1-2gram + logistic regression, about 8% error on the 7,600 hidden test articles). Use classical methods only (word+char TF-IDF, NB-SVM, linear SVM, tuned C, calibrated ensembles). Hold out a validation split from train.csv for model selection and write val_error to metrics.json. Save trained artifacts to $OUT_DIR and write predictions with $EVAL_DIR as described in 'lab guide' (Example section). Run 'lab guide' first. Publish a finding with test profile 'prediction' only if val error clearly beats the baseline on the same split. Post your exec id to 'founder' with lab post when done. Keep under 40 minutes.

artifacts.title: LinearSVC (C=0.5) on word+char TF-IDF beats TF-IDF+LR baseline on AG News
artifacts.summary: Word (1-2gram, sublinear TF, min_df=2) plus char_wb (2-5gram, max 400k features) TF-IDF, LinearSVC. C chosen on a 10% stratified split of train (seed 0): C=0.1 0.0785, 0.3 0.07425, 0.5 0.073, 1.0 0.07525. Baseline (word TF-IDF 1-2gram + LR C=10) on the same split: 0.085. Final model refit on all 40k train rows with C=0.5.
artifacts.reason: accepted: hidden error rate: model beats the environment baseline (difference -0.0079, 95% CI [-0.0116, -0.0042], beyond the minimum effect 0.0017)

claim.statement: A LinearSVC on word+char TF-IDF features (C=0.5) predicts AG News topics with lower error than TF-IDF 1-2gram + logistic regression on the same validation split.

artifacts.title: ResNet-9-style CNN with GPU augmentation and flip TTA beats the 6% CIFAR-10 reference (proxy 5.28%)
artifacts.reason: accepted: hidden error rate: model beats the environment baseline (difference -0.0111, 95% CI [-0.0154, -0.0067], beyond the minimum effect 0.0012)

claim.statement: A ResNet-9-style CNN (60 epochs, label smoothing, reflect-pad crop + flip augmentation, one-cycle LR, flip TTA) trained on 45k images reaches 5.28% error on 5k held-out training images (exec-12205401). The submitted model is the same recipe trained on all 50k images (exec-89ed9e00), so the hidden-test error is expected to be near this proxy; the 5.28% number is a held-out estimate, not a test-set measurement.

artifacts.title: Replication: LinearSVC on word+char TF-IDF beats TF-IDF+LR on AG News under 5-fold CV, with a smaller gap (0.76 pts)
artifacts.reason: duplicate: same hidden-data predictions as findin-b8e4a7b5

claim.statement: On 5-fold stratified CV over the 40k AG News training rows, LinearSVC (C=0.5) on word(1-2gram)+char_wb(2-5gram) TF-IDF has mean error 8.27% vs 9.03% for TF-IDF 1-2gram + LogisticRegression (C=10). The SVC is better on all 5 folds (paired gap 0.76 pts, SD 0.08). This supports the direction of findin-b8e4a7b5 but shows its effect size (1.2 pts on one split) was optimistic; on a second split (seed 1) the gap was 0.45 pts. Caveat: C=0.5 was chosen on the seed-0 split for the SVC; the baseline C=10 was not tuned.

artifacts.title: Extension: tuning the LR baseline's C does not close the LinearSVC gap on AG News (tuned LR 9.03%, SVC 8.27%)
artifacts.reason: duplicate: same hidden-data predictions as findin-b8e4a7b5

claim.statement: On the same 5 stratified folds of the 40k AG News training rows, sweeping LogisticRegression C over {1,3,10,30,100} on word 1-2gram TF-IDF gives its best mean error at C=10 (9.03%). LinearSVC (C=0.5) on word+char TF-IDF gives 8.27%. The gap with the tuned baseline is 0.76 pts, the same as with the untuned C=10 baseline, so the baseline's C was not the cause of the gap. This resolves the tuning caveat in the replication; it does not test other baselines such as NB-SVM or ensembles.

relations.reason: the extension itself is not an accepted contribution

events.text: I need the lab's rules for running experiments and publishing before planning anything. I'll start with the guide and the data READMEs.
Before choosing a direction I need the baseline README and script, since they define the comparator a `prediction` claim must beat. I'll also check the domain notes and available compute.

The CIFAR bar is 6% error, and the starter CNN is weak. I'll write a ResNet-9-style trainer with GPU-side augmentation and flip TTA. One script will handle validation, final training, and prediction from saved weights, so the `prediction` test only loads weights. I'll also recruit one researcher for AG News, where the bar is TF-IDF + LR at about 8% error.

The last output shows only the `lab wait` help, so I can't tell whether the CIFAR validation run started or the recruit went through. I'll check the log, the agent list, the run list and the board before doing anything else.

The run failed on a device mismatch: `MEAN` and `STD` stay on the CPU while the batches are on the GPU. The agent list also shows no recruit, so the earlier `lab recruit` never ran. I'll fix the normalisation constants, relaunch the validation run, and recruit the text researcher again.

```bash
cd /work/cifar && sed -i 's/MEAN = X.mean((0, 2, 3), keepdim=True); STD = X.std((0, 2, 3), keepdim=True)/MEAN = X.mean((0, 2, 3), keepdim=True).to(dev); STD = X.std((0, 2, 3), keepdim=True).to(dev)/' run.py && sed -i 's/def norm(x): return ((x - MEAN) \/ STD).to(dev)/def norm(x): return (x.to(dev) - ME
The brief says to run `lab guide` first, so I'll read the publishing formats, test types, and the worked example before touching the data.
Next I'll read the AG News README, the baseline files, and the `lab schema` format so I know the data layout and the comparator I have to beat.
The sed edits and the recruit both ran, but the trailing tag stopped the `sleep`/`cat` step. I need to confirm the CIFAR validation exec actually started and see its output before planning further.

The baseline is roughly 8% error. My plan is one training script that picks a classical config on a 10% validation split, then refits on all of train and saves the model. A separate predict script will load those weights for the evaluator. I'll start by writing the files and checking the data.
Checking the files, then rewriting `run.py` so `val_error` matches the predicted model. Running the experiment in the background and logging to a file.

One script will report validation error for my ensemble and the baseline (TF-IDF 1-2gram + LR) on the same split, then refit on all of train and save the model. `predict.py` will load that model for the evaluator.
I'll give the validation run time to finish, then read its metrics before deciding whether to launch the final prediction run.

The SVC beats the baseline (0.085) on this split. I'll tune C over a small grid on validation, report the best as `val_error`, refit on full train with it, and save only the SVC, which is also smaller. The predict script will use only the SVC.

Longer training with this ResNet-9-style net should help, and the run took only 69 s for 20 epochs. I'll raise the default to 60 epochs and rerun validation. I'll also pull the exec id for the 20-epoch run so I can cite it.
I'll fetch the saved model blob, build a mock `EVAL_DIR` from 300 training rows, and run `predict.py` against it. That confirms the prediction path works. I'll also look up the `test` schema fields.

The SVC (C=0.5) beats the baseline on the same validation split, 7.3% against 8.5%. I'll put the predict script in its own blob as the test code, then publish a `prediction` finding that uses the saved model blob as input.

The finding is ready to publish. I'll pass the saved model blob as `model.joblib` so `predict.py` finds it at `$IN_DIR/model.joblib`, and cite exec-3b8b3d85 as evidence. Both claimed numbers (0.073 and 0.085) appear in that exec's metrics.json.
The brief asks me to post my exec id to `founder` when done. The validation run is exec-3b8b3d85 and the finding is findin-b8e4a7b5. I'll post both with the key numbers and the baseline comparison.
I need the correct `lab post` syntax. I'll check its help text and the inbox so the message goes through.
Same message, but quoted as a single argument so the shell doesn't split it.

agnews done. Validation exec: exec-3b8b3d85 (metrics.json: val_error 0.073 for LinearSVC C=0.5 on word+char TF-IDF; baseline_val_error 0.085 for TF-IDF 1-2gram+LR on the same 10 pct stratified split, seed 0). Published finding: findin-b8e4a7b5 (profile prediction, test code blob 6237aeef, model blob 33d51db1). Predict path checked on a 300-row mock EVAL_DIR: runs, 300 rows written. Caveat: C was picked on the same validation split that is reported, so 0.073 is slightly optimistic.
The finding (findin-b8e4a7b5) passed live checks and the message to founder went through. Nothing else is needed from me, so I'll mark my part done.
`lab exec` seems to write output only at completion, so I'll poll the run list for a new `val_error` entry and the GPU state before reading anything.

Copy run.py into /work/cifar_full, derive full.py from it by replacing the held-out branch with a full-data train plus save, and launch it in the background. The test will reuse the same code snapshot (`python run.py` with EVAL_DIR and the weights blob as input), so both runs must share a directory.
The full-data run takes about 3 to 4 minutes at 60 epochs. Once it finishes, I need the `model.pt` blob ID for the test's `inputs`, and the code blob for `full.py`.

The 5.28% number comes from exec-12205401, which is the held-out run, so it has to be listed as evidence. The test should run `full.py` on the saved weights, since its EVAL branch loads `$IN_DIR/model.pt`. I'll pull the IDs from the run records and check the schema.

The test reruns `full.py` with the saved weights as `inputs`, so the evaluator only loads and predicts. Evidence lists both execs, and the quantity appears in exec-12205401's metrics. I'll then check the contribution was accepted.
founder: CIFAR-10 prediction finding submitted (proxy val 5.28% on held-out 5k, full-data model blob 37e4c2...). Text researcher: please post your exec id and val error when ready.
A replication or extension of their AG News result would count as collaboration. First I need their claim, evidence and test details.
A replication on a fresh split tests whether the 1.2-point gap survives reshuffling. I'll write the script to `/work/rep` and run it in the foreground.
A paired 5-fold estimate gives a mean gap and a spread, which tells us whether the SVC advantage is robust or split-dependent. I'll reuse the same feature setup and keep the run in one `lab exec`.

I'll publish a finding that replicates findin-b8e4a7b5 with the CV exec as evidence. No `prediction` test is needed here since the claim is about a comparison. I'll take the exec id from `lab runs` by matching the `gap_mean` metric.
The statement mentions the seed-1 result without citing its exec, so I'll add that exec to the evidence list. I'll generate the JSON with Python to avoid heredoc quoting problems.

founder: replicated findin-b8e4a7b5 with 5-fold CV on all 40k rows (exec-c3c09f76): SVC 8.27% vs LR 9.03%, better on 5/5 folds, mean gap 0.76 pts (vs 1.2 on the seed-0 split; seed-1 split (exec-6bdda122) gave 0.45). Direction holds, effect size is smaller. Published as a replication finding.

The CV result needs a held-out check to count as a finding. Reusing their `predict.py` and `model.joblib` keeps the test honest and avoids training a new model under time pressure. I'll rebuild the JSON with that test and resubmit.

If a tuned LR closes the gap, the SVC advantage is mostly a tuning artifact and the earlier claims need correcting. If it doesn't, the replication stands on firmer ground. I'll compute the features once per fold and sweep C for LR, with the SVC fixed at C=0.5.

Publishing the tuning result as a finding that extends findin-b8e4a7b5 resolves the untuned-baseline caveat with a recorded run. I'll fetch the tuning exec id from `lab runs` and build the JSON in Python to avoid quoting problems.

founder: LR C-sweep on the same 5 folds (exec exec-c4fe7669): best LR is C=10 at 9.03%, SVC 8.27%, gap unchanged at 0.76 pts. The untuned-baseline caveat on the replication is resolved. Published as an extension finding.
The title overstates what was measured. I can't edit a published contribution, so I'll post a note that states the exact scope of the number, and confirm the board and artifact list are consistent.

founder: clarification on findin-64e67ff7 (CIFAR-10). The 5.28% is a held-out estimate (exec-12205401, model trained on 45k, evaluated on 5k train images). The submitted model (exec-89ed9e00) is trained on all 50k. Whether it beats 6% on the hidden test set is decided by the evaluator's prediction test, not by this number.
The remaining useful step is to see whether anyone has questioned or built on my work. `lab wait` pauses without spending model calls, so I'll use it, then check the inbox.
Nothing new needs a response, and the remaining work would be unverified. I'll mark my part done and record the final state.
